prompt:

Write the requested response as one self-contained paragraph of plain text. Do not use a title, headings, bullet points, numbered lists, Markdown formatting, code fences, or line breaks. base_prompt: Explain the purpose of a software interface that hides complicated internal work behind a small set of actions. A response of around 160 words is enough.
text: A software interface provides a simple, consistent way for people or other programs to use a system without needing to understand its internal complexity. It exposes a small set of meaningful actions, such as saving a file, sending a message, processing a payment, or retrieving data, while hiding the many calculations, validations, storage operations, network requests, and error-handling steps required to complete them. This separation is useful because users can focus on their goals rather than implementation details. It also helps developers change or improve the internal design without forcing every user of the system to change their own code, as long as the interface remains stable. Clear interfaces reduce mistakes, make software easier to learn, support reuse, and allow teams to work independently on different parts of a product. In effect, the interface acts as a contract: it defines what actions are available, what information is needed, and what result or behavior can be expected.
